collectedVia: service-role SQL (trigger/function introspection + a deterministic behavioural clamp test on a throwaway, deleted in-block)
authorization: Follow-up to the user-authorized repid-engine griefing test; investigating the event-vs-live-score divergence it surfaced.
question: Is the divergence (event stores repid_after=990/repid_delta_applied=-10 while live current_repid stays 1000) an intended protection or a ledger bug?
answer: BOTH: a GOOD protective control (the earned floor) causes a LOW ledger-accuracy defect (the event overstates the applied penalty).

mechanism_verified.trigger: trg_repid_earned_floor — BEFORE UPDATE OF current_repid ON repid_agents
mechanism_verified.trigger_body: NEW.peak_repid := greatest(NEW.peak_repid, OLD.peak_repid, NEW.current_repid); v_floor := coalesce(NEW.floor_override, tier_lower_bound(NEW.peak_repid)); IF NEW.current_repid < v_floor THEN NEW.current_repid := v_floor; END IF;
mechanism_verified.two_floors_root_cause: The JS pipeline (src/scoring/pipeline.ts) writes the event's repid_after/repid_delta_applied from its own applyToScore()+clampRepidLoud(), which clamps to a GLOBAL REPID_MIN. It then UPDATEs repid_agents.current_repid=new_repid, which the DB trigger re-clamps to the PEAK-based tier_lower_bound(peak_repid). When tier_lower_bound(peak) > REPID_MIN, the two disagree and only the DB one binds — so the event records movement against the wrong (looser) floor.

reconciliation_tripwire_blindspot: appliedScoreReconciles() checks the JS decomposition's internal consistency (before + decay + delta + clamp == after); it does NOT compare the JS after against the post-trigger live current_repid, so it cannot catch this class.
severity: Low — audit/ledger-accuracy, not exploitable; arises from a PARTIAL control (the earned floor CAPS a griefing drain at the floor — corrected 2026-08-17: it does NOT zero it; 164/176 agents have a drainable gap above their floor, REPID-ENG-001). But repid_score_events cannot be summed to reconstruct current_repid, and repid_delta_applied overstates movement at/near the earned floor.
recommended_fix: Make the JS applier clamp to the same floor the DB trigger uses — coalesce(floor_override, tier_lower_bound(peak_repid)) — so the event's repid_after/repid_delta_applied equal the actual post-trigger movement; or store BOTH calculated and true-applied (post-clamp) with distinct labels. The DB trigger is the source of truth; the event should mirror it.
